newsitem.title: JAPAN: Global cell phone market grows 57% in '96 - report.
newsitem.headline: Global cell phone market grows 57% in '96 - report.

text.p: Global shipments of cellular phones totalled 66 million units in calendar 1996, up 57 percent from the previous year, market research firm Dataquest Inc said.
Shipments are expected to rise 29 percent year-on-year to 85 million units in 1997, it said in a report.
More than 60 percent of the phones will be based on digital technology, said the report, released on Tuesday.
In 1996, shipments of digital mobile phones totalled 36.9 million units, up from 1.3 million units in 1995. Shipments of analog mobile phones totalled 29.1 million last year.
Japan showed the fastest growth of any market amid fierce competition among providers of cell phone services, including those offering the Personal Handyphone System (PHS), the report said.
PHS, developed in Japan, has a shorter range than other systems but the phones are cheaper to use than conventional portable phones.

With total shipments of 17.2 million units, Motorola Inc continued to hold the largest share of 26.0 percent in the global cell phone market in 1996, although its share slipped from the previous year's 30.8 percent due to the rapid growth of the digital phone market, Dataquest said.
Second-ranked Finnish telecoms group Nokia Oy's market share declined to 20.4 percent in 1996 from 23.1 percent in 1995 due to sluggish sales in Japan.

Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd was the top Japanese company with a five percent global market share in 1996, ranking fourth on the list, helped by its strong growth in digital cellular markets.
Other Japanese cell phone makers such as NEC Corp, Mitsubishi Electric Corp and Kyocera Corp also expanded their global market shares due to growth in the Japanese market.
Dataquest said shipments of cell phones based on analog technology peaked in 1996 and that the market would shift to digital cell phones.

The Asian cellular phone market is likely to show the fastest growth this calendar year at 47 percent, compared with North American's forecast 28 percent growth and Europe's 24 percent growth, it said.
